official capacity, creating actual or potential loopholes for impunity.","notes":["The excerpt supports incomplete coverage of the Convention definition, including discrimination and official-capacity actors, but does not specifically support the summary’s wording about purposes beyond extracting confessions."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E011","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The excerpt recommends ensuring that, where torture is alleged, the burden of proof remains with the procuratorate and courts and that allegations are promptly and properly investigated.","notes":["The excerpt is a recommendation and does not support the proposed claims that courts often shifted the burden, dismissed exclusion requests, or that China supplied no statistics."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E012","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E014","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E015","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E016","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E017","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The excerpt urges China to establish a moratorium on executions, commute existing death sentences, and refrain from automatically imposing restraints on death-row prisoners.","notes":["The excerpt does not support the proposed claim that the Committee welcomed ending the death penalty for some economic and non-lethal crimes, nor the specific report about 24-hour shackling."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E018","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E019","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The excerpt calls for victims and their families connected with the 1989 events to obtain full reparation and for relevant legal safeguards and due-process rights to be respected.","notes":["The supplied excerpt does not establish that the Committee found the allegations had not been independently investigated or that the State party characterized the suppression as necessary and correct."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E020","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E021","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The Committee reported that claims for State compensation were statute-barred within two years from when the plaintiff knew or should have known of the damage, and regretted the lack of information on whether a formal proactive rehabilitation mechanism existed.","notes":["The excerpt supports the two-year limitation period and missing information about a formal proactive mechanism, but does not establish that no such mechanism was documented as a fact."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0027-R01-E022","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
